source_quality.text_layer: usable prose; formula glyphs lost to legacy encoding and recovered from the page rasters; the text layer swaps the numerators of equations (1) and (2)

task_reconstruction: Prioritize the 17 SDGs, plan their ten-year development, and show how the network changes when a goal is achieved, a goal is added, or a crisis strikes.

section_map.summary: summary: the two networks, the ranking, the forecast, the crises, the generalization
introduction: background and the five tasks
definitions, three assumptions, the notation table
indicator edges and goal edges by the coefficient of variation
five priority indicators and the entropy-weighted score
the ARIMA forecast with the priority term
removing a finished goal and adding a new one
international crises, with forest fires worked through
the six general steps and the interface
sensitivity of the three ARIMA orders

contributions.summary: a goal network generated automatically from an indicator network
a priority score from five network measures with data-driven weights
node removal and node addition as defined updates of the same network

assumptions.summary: a goal is achieved when its indicators reach the optimal value and stay there, because swinging about the target means instability
nodes affect each other within months or a year, because coordination ties the departments together
statistical properties stay predictable, because the main drivers are steady over a short term

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 241 official indicators, 2000-2022, from three named official databases
rescaling against the official optimal value, with a negative result floored at zero
indicators ranked by total absolute correlation, the top ones kept

models.summary: normalization against the optimal value, equations (1)-(2)
indicator network and goal network, equations (3)-(11)
priority score from five network measures, equations (12)-(21)
ARIMA forecast plus a priority term, equations (22)-(23)

verification.summary: the ranking is compared with the Copenhagen Consensus Center order
removing the first goal produces a new printed top five
the three orders are chosen on a 2016-2020 hold-out

results_trace.summary: the top five are goals 17, 3, 1, 4 and 13, with scores from 6.2875 down to 5.4183
the first goal is called achievable within ten years
removing the first goal brings goals 6 and 10 into the top five

writing_logic.summary: the summary moves first, next, furthermore, meanwhile, finally, one paragraph per task
the five tasks are numbered with the same five markers
the crisis section ends by assigning the body a duty to notice and adapt

language_observations.summary: the model is justified by a moral aim: to make the world a better place, we develop
a weight direction is defended by a chain: larger gap means harder, so greater weight
a known measure is adapted with the reason first: since the graph is complete, we modify
the weakness is put on the user: we cannot guarantee, and lacking input causes deviation

visualization_observations.summary: figure 7: the goal network with one goal's edges highlighted and weights from 0 to 10
figure 8: the mapping from the indicator network to the goal network
figures 10 and 11: poverty and life expectancy with the priority term added
figure 19: the forecast against the real values as the order p varies

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: a judge looking for a usable plan gets a named top five, a ten-year reading and a worked crisis
the ranking is checked against a published order, which is the comparison a judge can verify

weaknesses.summary: equation (8) reuses j as both the indicator index and the sum index
equation (20) sums over i not equal to j while i is the free index
the entropy derivation behind equation (21) is never written
no cutoff is given for how many indicators a goal keeps
the 95 percent energy claim has no table behind it
the crises are argued in prose and the network is never recomputed
the result depends on a user who fully understands the goals and indicators

independent_extensions.summary: a proposed eighteenth goal, access to information and communication technologies, argued from three indicators

unresolved_questions: why the text layer swaps the numerators of equations (1) and (2)
why equation (8) reuses j for the indicator and the sum
why equation (14) sums over the zero diagonal
why equation (20) sums over i not equal to j
why the entropy formulas are never shown
why no cutoff is given for how many indicators are kept
why the 95 percent energy claim has no table
why the crises are not rerun through the network
why p, d and q are chosen without a reported error
